subject: Demo debrief — candidate model slate, trade-offs, and sprint asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Demo debrief — candidate model slate, trade-offs, and sprint asks

Team — quick recap from the call with Amy (LumenHealth) this morning and my recommended next steps. I wrote up a short slate of candidate models with pragmatic trade-offs; the attached artifacts include the raw benchmark CSV and the prompt pack we used in the demo.

High-level takeaways from the LumenHealth demo:
- Use case: clinical summarization + EHR-aware Q&A (short to medium context, strict hallucination risk). They prioritize factuality > sub-second tail latency.
- Traffic shape: expected bursty interactive traffic (100–250 reqs/min on day 1 for pilot) with 95thpct latency SLO of ~600ms for the baseline flows.
- Budget: pilot prefers hosted with a hard cost cap; procurement will evaluate reserved capacity for scale.

Recommended candidate slate (shortlist, prioritized):
1) rw-mistral-7b-q8 (recommended pilot)
   - Rationale: best balance for the use case — strong instruction-following and factuality on our finetuned clinical adapters, median latency ~220ms on T4p-like tier (demo config), token cost low.
   - Trade-offs: Slightly lower pass-rate on complex multi-hop clinical reasoning tests vs bigger models; we mitigate with targeted prompt templates in prompt_pack_v1.

2) rw-llama-13b-qdq (fallback / quality-first)
   - Rationale: higher quality on difficult summarization and long-context cross-document linkage; median latency ~410ms on the same host, higher token cost but fewer retries.
   - Trade-offs: Cost and operational memory footprint; good candidate for reserved capacity if they prioritize correctness over unit cost.

3) rw-sta-70b-8bit (quality ceiling, limited pilot)
   - Rationale: Best-in-class for edge-case factuality and multi-document glue. Use behind canary routing for 5–10% of traffic to validate regression risk.
   - Trade-offs: Latency ~800ms median unless we use larger instances; significantly higher $/token. Consider only if they accept higher spend for improved recall.

Benchmarks referenced in attachment: latency_cost_matrix.csv (latency P50/P95 with cost estimates); benchmarks_20270924.pdf has side-by-side qualitative evals (ROUGE/QA accuracy on clinical prompt set). Also linked the evaluation dashboard above.

Quality/regression guardrails and prompts:
- The prompt pack includes: canonical instruction templates, entity-preserving system messages, and negative examples with explicit "do not hallucinate" constraints. We should run these prompts across the three models for a quick regression snapshot.
- Action: Soojin, can you run the prompt_pack_v1.jsonl against the rw-llama-13b-qdq and rw-mistral-7b-q8 configs (same token limits) and produce a 1-page pass/fail summary for the top 20 prompts? Deadline: Tue EOD PT (2027-09-28).

Commercial & ops asks:
- Ben: can you produce a 30/90/180-day cost projection for hosted vs reserved capacity for the pilot (assume 200 reqs/min bursts, average completion 180 tokens)? We need 2 options: hosted with soft caps, and a reserved 1-month commit.
- Marissa: please confirm we can share the SOC2 summary and the SOW template for procurement next week.

Next customer-facing step: propose a two-week pilot on rw-mistral-7b-q8 (pilot traffic routed to rw-llama-13b-qdq as fallback for low-confidence outputs). Ask the customer to pick top-2 models they'd like evaluated in the pilot. I will draft the pilot plan and include the canary routing config.

Thanks — Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Group Product Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: benchmarks_20270924.pdf (report), prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (prompts), latency_cost_matrix.csv (benchmark CSV)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 15:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo debrief — candidate model slate, trade-offs, and sprint asks

All good — agree with the prioritization. Two quick asks from my side:
1) Cost table: I will build a simple hosted vs reserved delta using the attached latency_cost_matrix.csv. Expect numbers by EOD Monday (2027-09-27).
2) Regression monitoring: we should define a concrete regression metric (e.g., clinical QA F1 drop >4% or hallucination count). If we gate rollouts on that, we avoid surprises.

I'll add a line item for fallback routing (auto-failover to 13b when model confidence < 0.45) and estimate the incremental requests routed.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amy Rivera <amy@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2027 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: LumenHealth pilot — recommended candidate models and next asks

Hi Amy — thanks again for the demo today. Good discussion; we captured the constraints and have a recommended cadence for a short pilot. Below is a short, non-technical summary for procurement and clinical ops, plus the attachments we ran in the demo.

Summary recommendation (pilot):
- Primary candidate: rw-mistral-7b-q8 — lowest latency and cost while preserving strong factuality with our clinical adapter.
- Secondary candidate (fallback): rw-llama-13b-qdq — higher accuracy on edge cases; used as a fallback for low-confidence outputs.
- Quality ceiling (optional canary): rw-sta-70b-8bit — for validating difficult edge-case transcripts.

Attachments included: benchmarks_20270924.pdf, prompt_pack_v1.jsonl, latency_cost_matrix.csv. The prompt pack contains the exact prompts we used during the demo including a red-team prompt set for hallucination checks.

Request: could you (or procurement) indicate which two models you'd like to pilot (primary + fallback)? If feasible, please add procurement@lumenhealth.com to the thread so we can coordinate the SOW and SOC2 evidence exchange.

We can also provide a short sample of model outputs for two anonymized clinical transcripts if that would help clinical ops evaluate immediate quality — happy to run that and include a brief comparison.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Group Product Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Amy Rivera <amy@lumenhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: LumenHealth pilot — recommended candidate models and next asks

Hi Hannah — thanks for the quick follow-up and the materials. This is super helpful. Two quick requests from our side before we confirm the pilot models:
1) Can you share 3–5 side-by-side response examples (redacted PHI) for the mistral 7b q8 vs the 13b qdq on the clinical transcript prompts? That will help our clinical team evaluate hallucination patterns.
2) Procurement asks: please share the SOC2 summary and a draft SOW (scope, pilot duration, termination clauses, and estimated spend). I added procurement@lumenhealth.com to the thread.

If those look good we'll aim to kick off the pilot the week of Oct 11. For now, please send the sample outputs and the SOC2/SOW drafts and I'll route to the clinical lead.

—Amy Rivera
Product Lead, Clinical Workflows
LumenHealth
